binders: Two measures mu and nu on the Borel real line.
conclusions: Agreement of mu and nu on every lower closed interval implies mu = nu.
Equality mu = nu implies agreement on every lower closed interval.
mathematical_definitions: Measure evaluation returns an extended nonnegative real.
A probability measure has total mass one.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Two Borel probability measures on the real line are equal exactly when they assign the same mass to every lower closed interval.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is restricted to probability measures on the Borel real line.
Agreement is required at every real threshold and specifically on inclusive lower intervals.
The reverse implication is immediate; the substantive direction is uniqueness.
Probability measures on the real line exist, so the statement is nonvacuous.
